nodes.summary: A real number $x$ has an eventually periodic continued fraction if and only if $x$ is a real quadratic irrational.
nodes.title: Euler–Lagrange theorem

nodes.summary: If a real number $x$ is a real quadratic irrational, then the continued fraction of $x$ is eventually periodic.
nodes.title: Lagrange's theorem on periodic continued fractions

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a real number with regular continued fraction $[a_0; a_1, a_2, \dots]$. The continued fraction of $x$ is eventually periodic if it does not terminate and its sequence of partial denominators $(a_n)_{n \ge 1}$, which omits the head coefficient $a_0$, is eventually periodic: there are natural numbers $p > 0$ and $n_0 \ge 1$ such that $a_{n+p} = a_n$ for every $n \ge n_0$.
nodes.title: Eventually periodic continued fractions

nodes.summary: If the continued fraction of a real number $x$ is eventually periodic, then $x$ is a real quadratic irrational.
nodes.title: Euler's theorem on periodic continued fractions

nodes.summary: A real number $x$ is a real quadratic irrational if it is integral (equivalently, algebraic) over $\mathbb{Q}$ and its minimal polynomial over $\mathbb{Q}$ has degree $2$.
nodes.title: Real quadratic irrationals
